compliance.emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; EN 62479; EN 50663

features.antenna: an active GNSS antenna is required - 50 ohm impedance match, 5 V DC, noise figure 1.5 dB maximum, internal LNA gain 35-42 dB (HIG Installing an Antenna)
features.gnss: internal GNSS receiver for master-clock implementations; edge Grandmaster with PRTC
features.optics-qsfp-dd: 400G QSFP-DD SR/LR/ER/ZR/OpenZR+, up to 600 km (datasheet port table)
features.optics-sfp28: 25G SFP28 SR/LR/ER up to 40 km; 10G SFP+ SR/LR/ER; 1G SFP SX/LX/EX
features.sfp28-sharing: the four SFP28 ports are in-band port share with 100GE port 0 (datasheet)
features.timing: Stratum 3E OCXO, ITU-T SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 with an additional licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC, Time Sensitive Networking; NOS integration is required to activate any of it
features.timing-cable: 50 ohm SMA coaxial with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS, 50 ohm SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz, shielded RJ45 for ToD (datasheet Compatible Timing Cable Types)
features.timing-interfaces: GNSS in on SMA, 10MHz in/out on SMB, 1PPS in/out on SMB, ToD in/out on RJ45

management.console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console

configs.description: The chassis as HIG Figure 7's rear elevation draws it - four FAN-803816-HI exhaust fans and two PSU-202-AESR 2000 W AC supplies with portrait C20 inlets and red latches, front-to-back airflow, and the sixty traffic and management ports empty. The HIG rates the feed at 200-240 V and notes that on a single 110 VAC source each supply delivers 1000 W. No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document; see the chassis-sku gap.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: Dual 2000 W DC supplies (PSU-202-DESR, two-post screw terminal under a hinged plastic cover, red latch) with the same FAN-803816-HI exhaust fans. This is the build the vendor's rear product photograph shows. Datasheet input -40 to -72 V at 60 A; the HIG's DC section gives the maximum system consumption as 1497 W against the AC build's 1483.3 W.
configs.name: dc

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Each QSFP28 port carries a four-lamp cluster in the printed band above or below its block and each QSFP-DD port a lamp in one of the four blue light-pipe strips; nothing states what any of them means, nor - for the QSFP-DD strips - which of a strip's two lamps serves which of the two ports on that row. The lamp-to-port pairing written here is derived from the count alone (eight lamps, eight ports, taken left to right) and is the one thing in this device's LED model that is not read off a source. Every lamp keeps the component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up, down and passing traffic

gaps.note: The two lamps in the out-of-band jack's aperture are drawn green in HIG Figure 8 and are modelled, but THIS guide tables them nowhere. The link/activity vocabulary they carry is borrowed from the S9510-28DC and S9311-64D hardware guides, whose Management Port LED tables give 1G green on the left and 10M/100M amber on the right for the same class of jack on the same vendor's boxes. That is an inference from a sibling document and is recorded as one rather than being left to look sourced.
gaps.wanted: a management-port LED table in a later revision of this guide

gaps.note: HIG Figure 8 prints every port numeral on the schematic module face, where a seated transceiver would cover it, and the datasheet's product render of the same panel with the cages empty shows no numeral anywhere on the metal at 7x. The NUMBERING is certain and is used throughout; where the vendor actually prints it - on the bezel frame, on the EMI strip, or nowhere at all - is not established, so no numerals are drawn.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on high-resolution photograph of the faceplate with the cages empty

gaps.note: Same measure, same scope, two values, so it is filed rather than reconciled. The HIG's Component Physical Information table gives the PSU 321 mm deep; HIG Figures 5 and 6, the vendor's own mechanical drawings of the AC and DC units, both dimension the body at 360.0 mm and 369.8 mm over the handle. Nothing in this model depends on it - a module's `size` is its face - but a rack depth budget would.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace PSU-202 datasheet, or a revision of the HIG that reconciles its own table

gaps.note: FAN-803816-HI is ordered by both this router and the S9600-28DX and the two guides dimension it differently: the S9600-28DX HIG gives 80 x 113 x 81.5 mm and this one gives 80 x 122 x 80 mm for the same part number. Width agrees; depth differs by 9 mm and face height by 1.5 mm. The component carries the 28DX figures because that is where it was built and where its art was measured, and this device reuses it unchanged rather than forking a second contract off a one-line table difference.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FRU datasheet for FAN-803816-HI

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says the grounding location 'is covered with a protective label' and step 5 says to remove it, but neither the rear elevation nor the rear product photograph shows a label there - both draw a bare silver two-hole plate. The plate is modelled as the two images show it. Whether the shipped unit has a label over it, and what colour, is not established here.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of an unopened unit's rear panel

gaps.note: No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document. The datasheet's Available to Order block lists the PSU and fan SKUs only, and the HIG names the product S9600-56DX in its title, its overview and its dimensions table without printing a number. The configurations here therefore carry no `part-numbers`. The S9510-28DC's history is the warning: 'no SKU exists' was written there on exactly this evidence and was false, so this says only that we hold no document naming one.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or price list for the S9600 aggregation line

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

a top-level `profile:` naming the device class, so that `specified` has something to judge the attrs against - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml for the classes that exist, which unlocks `specified` and with it the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, qsfpdd-400g, sfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

provenance.attrs: datasheet - Specifications, Environmental, Performance, Regulatory Compliance and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied.
provenance.chassis: datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm or 17.17" x 30" x 3.45"', 'Weight: 19.26kg or 42.46lb (without FRU)'; the HIG's Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple and the same weight. 436 is the body and not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance paragraph states both numbers in one sentence - 'The S9600-56DX width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks' - so the ears are the 46.7 mm difference and are not drawn. Figure 8 corroborates it by drawing two small bracket tabs standing OUTSIDE the full-height body on each side (px 6-10 and 1384-1390 against a body of 11-1383). 87.7 mm is 1.98 rack units, which is why the datasheet calls it 2RU. The 762 mm depth is the chassis without FRUs; the HIG adds that the fan handles project 29 mm and the PSU handles 30 mm, which is clearance rather than body and is carried on those components' relief instead.
provenance.connector-orientation: photo/drawing, measured rather than assumed, and it comes out OPPOSITE to the S9311-64D's. Each 2x2 assembly is one belly-to-belly ganged cage: the luminance profile at figure x 303-312 shows the upper port's graded bezel band BELOW its face (y 78-84) and the lower port's ABOVE its face (y 90-100), with the white perforated EMI strip between them at y 85-89. The two rows therefore mirror, detail facing the strip. std/qsfp-ganged, std/qsfp-dd and std/sfp-ganged all draw their cage lip near the TOP of the opening, so the UPPER port of every pair is rotate: 180 and the lower is unrotated - that is grid rows 1 and 3 rotated, and rows 2 and 4 not, which is the reverse of ufispace/s9311-64d and is stated here so nobody 'fixes' one to match the other. The USB 3.0 socket is PORTRAIT (its drawn silver shell is 6.0 wide by 13.2 tall) so std/usb-a is rotated 90.
provenance.front-grid: drawing - the whole faceplate sits on ONE four-row grid, which is the finding that made the rest of this face cheap. Taking the pitch from a feature that repeats once per PORT rather than from the drawn cage bezels: a column profile through the left block (figure x 303-312) reads a flat luminance-150 module face at y 53-77, 102-126, 151-174 and 199-222, so row centres are 65, 113.5, 162 and 210.5 px - a uniform 48.5 px, 15.58 mm, with no interval more than 0.5 px off it. The BANDS that the eye reads (rows 1-2 as one assembly, rows 3-4 as another) are the white EMI strip between the first pair and the dark chassis web between the second and third rows; the pitch does not change. In millimetres the four row centres are 19.276, 34.856, 50.436 and 66.016. THE QSFP-DD PORTS SHARE THE SAME GRID: their flat faces read 115 and 161.5 px against the grid's 113.5 and 162, half a millimetre, so they are carried on rows 2 and 3 rather than given a second set of numbers.
provenance.grounding: HIG section 8 - the router is grounded through a #6 AWG two-hole lug and M4 screws supplied in the kit, and the guide says 'The location for securing the grounding lug is at the rear of the case and is covered with a protective label' and later 'remove the protective label'. ONE location, not two. The rear elevation and the rear photograph both show that location as a bare silver two-hole plate with an earth symbol beside it - no yellow label on either, unlike the S9311-64D whose figure draws the label in place - so the plate is drawn as the metal both images show and the label's absence is noted here rather than invented onto the panel. Plate at x 348.6-357.8, y 4.98-38.87 with its two holes at y centres 9.0 and 25.2; the earth symbol at x 361.6-366.6, y 17.6-22.3.
provenance.legends: drawing, positions measured, wording read where it resolves and taken from the HIG's own callouts where it does not. Readable at 4-6x: 1PPS, 10MHZ, GNSS ANT, TOD, RESET, the S9600-56DX wordmark at the bottom right and the 0/1..0/4 pair legends on the yellow band. Not readable and taken from HIG Figure 4's callout list instead: the two IOIOI console marks and the network symbol under the management jack. The six system lamps' names are the HIG Front Panel LED table's own row order - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID - printed on a white block at x 6.67-10.16, y 55.90-70.99 with the lamps in a column immediately to its right at 2.51 mm pitch, the same construction the S9311-64D uses. THE YELLOW AND ORANGE BANDS ARE REAL PAINT, not figure highlighting: the datasheet's product render shows the same yellow band with the same orange sub-band under it. What they MEAN is not stated - the datasheet's only related sentence is that the four SFP28 ports are 'In-band port share with 100GE Port 0' - so they are drawn and not interpreted. A small hazard triangle sits at the yellow/orange boundary in both images and is NOT drawn, because nothing states what it warns of.
provenance.lifecycle: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9600-56DX end of life' - no announcement found; the vendor's telco aggregation product page and the hardware installation guide are both live. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.
provenance.panel-metal: THE BRIGHT SHELL AROUND EACH GANGED BLOCK IS PANEL, NOT PART. The datasheet's product render (fig-0003) shows the real thing with the cages EMPTY: six dark apertures per block sitting inside a bright bezel frame with a perforated EMI strip between the rows. std/ parts draw the opening and stop, so each 2x2 assembly is drawn here as one light decor rectangle with the apertures placed on it - upper QSFP28 band y 13.49-39.51, lower 45.29-71.31, QSFP-DD 28.59-54.61, each 26.02 mm tall, with x and width per assembly measured off the same figure y 80 band. Without them the cages sit invisibly on a dark faceplate. The same reasoning puts a gold disc behind each coax jack (std/sma and std/smb draw the bore, not the knurled nut), a silver shell behind the portrait USB 3.0 socket and behind the micro-USB, and a white rectangle under the six system-lamp legends, which the figure prints dark on a printed white block.
provenance.port-leds: drawing - and the arrangement differs per family, which is why it was counted rather than assumed. QSFP28: a green printed band runs above the upper assemblies and below the lower ones, carrying FOUR round lamps per port in TWO rows per column - colour detection returns 4 lamps per column at figure y 30-33 and 4 more at y 41-44, on a 12.8 px (4.07 mm) pitch, repeated in the bottom band at y 233-236 and 244-247. That is one four-lamp cluster per port, so ufispace/lane-led-quad (14.4 x 2.6, 3.94 mm pitch) is placed 48 times: grid rows 1 and 2 in the upper band's two lamp rows, rows 3 and 4 in the lower band's. QSFP-DD: four blue light-pipe strips instead, at figure x 684-695 and 965-976 and split into an upper and a lower element per side, each carrying two green lamps (y 115.5/125 and 151.5/161.5). Eight lamps for eight ports, which is the count this model uses - WHICH lamp serves which of the two ports in a strip's row is NOT stated anywhere and is recorded in the port-led-semantics gap. White diamond light pipes stand at each cage assembly's ends inside the green bands (figure x 414-422 and 427-435 at the first internal boundary, singles at the block ends) and are drawn as decor.
provenance.port-numbers: NOT DRAWN, deliberately, and this is a positive finding rather than an omission. HIG Figure 8 numbers every port - 0-47 in green, 48-55 in blue, 0/1-0/4 in orange - but prints each numeral ON the schematic module face, where a seated transceiver would cover it. The datasheet's product render of the same panel with the cages EMPTY (fig-0003) shows no numeral anywhere on the metal: the bright bezel frames and the EMI strips are unmarked at 7x. So the NUMBERING is certain and is used for every id and rel-pos here; where the vendor prints it is recorded as a gap. The 0/1..0/4 pair legends ARE on the metal - they sit on the yellow band above the SFP28 block, outside the cages - and are drawn.
provenance.power: datasheet 'Typical power: 481 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG's Connecting Power sections state the maximum twice, once per build: 1497 W for DC and 1483.3 W for AC, and unlike the typical figure these ARE qualified, in a note printed beside them - 'Temperature: 45C, Optics: fully populated, Traffic: 100% load', with OpenZR+ transceivers on selected ports. 1497 is carried as power-max-w because max means the highest of the two builds, and the 13.7 W difference is recorded here rather than as a conflict: they are two builds, not two readings. Note that power-envelope therefore describes the TYPICAL figure's scope and not the maximum's, which is fully-configured and says so in this sentence. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set: the fans publish no draw at all, so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor. Provisioning reserve 2000 W per circuit (HIG). PSU rating 2000 W per supply from the ordering lines; on a single 110 VAC feed the HIG derates each supply to 1000 W.
provenance.psu-build: THE GUIDE DRAWS ONE BUILD AND THE PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS THE OTHER, and both are modelled. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation draws the AC supply (a portrait C20 inlet with a cord clip, vent grid on the LEFT, lamp 8.5 mm from the bay's left edge); the rear product photograph shows the DC supply (a two-post screw terminal under a hinged plastic cover on the LEFT, vent grid and lamp on the RIGHT at 37.5 mm). They are not two readings of one face - they are two faces, laid out opposite ways round, and the datasheet orders both: PSU-202-AESR and PSU-202-DESR, 2000 W each, exhaust airflow. The AC build is the default here because it is the one the vendor's own elevation draws, and the DC build is a configuration. Neither is a gap; what IS a gap is the PSU depth, which the HIG's table and the HIG's own PSU drawing state differently.
provenance.qsfp28-layout: drawing - twelve columns in two blocks of six. Cage bezel edges read off a clean band at figure y 80 give left-block centres 330.0, 393.0, 457.5, 521.0, 585.5 and 648.5 px (least-squares 329.72 + 63.814k, no residual over 1.5 px) and right-block centres 1009, 1073, 1137.5, 1201, 1265.5 and 1330 px (1008.90 + 64.171k). In millimetres that is 101.21 + 20.264k and 316.88 + 20.377k. THE PITCH IS ITS OWN CHECK: 20.3 mm is the published ganged-QSFP cage pitch, arrived at here from a figure that was not set by it. The drawn bezel is 19.8 mm wide, so the registry's 18.5 mm std/qsfp-ganged aperture is centred on each column and the 1.3 mm of bright shell either side is drawn as panel decor - see panel-metal. Numbering is COLUMN-MAJOR and is Figure 8's own: port = 4 x column + row, so the left block's first column carries 0, 1, 2, 3 top to bottom and the last column of the right block carries 44, 45, 46, 47.
provenance.qsfpdd-layout: drawing - two 2x2 assemblies in the middle of the panel, column centres 728, 792, 868 and 931 px (227.68, 248.01, 272.14 and 292.14 mm), on rows 2 and 3 of the shared grid. Within an assembly the pitch is 20.3 and 20.0 mm, matching the QSFP28 blocks; between the two assemblies there is a 24.1 mm step with a vented chassis web in it. Numbering is Figure 8's: port = 48 + 2 x column + row, giving 48/50 over 49/51 in the left assembly and 52/54 over 53/55 in the right. std/qsfp-dd (19.0 x 10.0) is centred on each cell.
provenance.rear-layout: drawing - HIG Figure 7's rear elevation at 3.039 px/mm across and 3.010 down. Four fan faces on an 84.47 mm pitch, read off the four green status lamps (figure x 71.6, 328.0, 585.0, 841.7 - three intervals of 256.5, 257.0, 256.5 px), and anchored through ufispace/fan-803816-hi's own lamp position (9.1, 20.5 within its 80 x 81.5 face) to put the first bay at x 9.20, y 2.56. THE PITCH WAS THEN MEASURED AGAIN IN A DIFFERENT IMAGE: the rear photograph, 948 px across the body at 2.174 px/mm, puts the same four lamps on an 84.4 mm pitch. Then a 5 mm chassis strip, the grounding column (a silver two-hole plate, an earth symbol, a captive screw and the FAN 0|1|2|3 position key), and the two PSU bays stacked at x 375.0, 50.5 wide and 40.2 tall, with PSU0 over PSU1. The bay legends PSU0 and PSU1 are chassis silkscreen: which bay is 0 is a position fact and cannot live on an interchangeable FRU.
provenance.scale-crosscheck: the two front images were measured independently and agree on SPAN but not on ORIGIN, and both readings are recorded rather than one being quietly preferred. HIG Figure 8 puts the four port-LED lamp rows at 8.51, 12.05, 73.72 and 77.26 mm from its own top edge; the datasheet render puts them at 9.74, 12.99, 75.11 and 78.36. Top-to-bottom span 68.75 against 68.62 mm - 0.13 mm across 436 mm of panel, which is as close as two independently drawn figures get. The whole difference is a 1.2 mm constant offset, which is 1.5 px at the render's own 1.243 px/mm and therefore inside its edge uncertainty, so the HIG figure's origin is the one carried here. A reader who re-measures the render and finds everything 1.2 mm low has found this sentence, not an error.
provenance.sfp28-block: drawing - a 2x2 assembly at figure x 169-283, y 46-128 with a white cross divider at x 227 and y 87, so column centres 59.22 and 77.64 mm and row centres 19.60 and 33.09 mm. THE DRAWN CELL IS 18.1 x 12.8 mm AND THE STANDARD OPENING IS 14.25 x 10.4, which is not reconciled and should not be: std/sfp-ganged is the registry part and is placed centred on the measured centres, so the block's outer extent and each port's centre are the figure's while the aperture is the standard's. The 27% surplus in the drawn width is the one place on this face where the figure and the registry disagree by more than a millimetre, and the registry wins for an opening size. Numbering is column-major like the rest: 0/1 over 0/2 in the left column, 0/3 over 0/4 in the right.
provenance.sources: UfiSpace S9600-56DX datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/converted/s9600-56dx-datasheet) for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9600-56DX Hardware Installation Guide (s9600-56dx-hig) for the faceplate and rear figures, the FRU dimension table, the LED tables, the rack attachment-pin count, the space clearances and grounding; three vendor product images (photos/s9600-56dx-1-angle, -2-front, -3-rear) for colour, counts and construction. Figure quality was gated before anything was measured. HIG Figure 8 (the port overview, fig-0015) measures 1373 x 273 px body against the datasheet's 436 x 87.7 mm - aspect 5.029 against a true 4.9715, 1.16% out - so it is orthographic enough to carry geometry and is the front ruler at 3.1491 px/mm across and 3.113 px/mm down, the two axes taken separately so the 1.16% anisotropy is absorbed rather than ignored. HIG Figure 7 (fan overview, fig-0014) carries the rear elevation above two fan isometrics; its rear FACE (below the lid band, y 55-318) measures 1325 x 264 px, aspect 5.019, 0.96% out, and is the rear ruler at 3.039 / 3.010 px/mm. The 549 px datasheet front render (fig-0003) is 1.243 px/mm and the 520 px front photograph 1.19 px/mm; both were used for colour, counts, construction and confirmation only.
provenance.views: Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and HIG Figure 4's footprint drawing, which prints the fan handles at the top of the panel. Seven long stadium recesses run across the lid; their spacing is proportioned off that drawing and is ESTIMATED, because the drawing's own aspect (370 x 739 px against 436 x 762 mm, 12.5% out) fails the figure gate and only fractions along one axis may be taken from it. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position - no held figure shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): each side carries the five rail attachment pins the HIG's rack mounting section counts - 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins' - plus the M4 screw that locks the inner rail, 'two M4 screws (one on each chassis side)'. The COUNT is the vendor's; every POSITION on both side faces is ESTIMATED, because no held figure dimensions them. Both side faces carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by any asymmetric feature.
